item.title: Nearly 2 out of 3 teens and tweens use AI chatbots, new research shows
item.description: Most kids say they use chatbots for help with homework and when they're stressed, lonely, or anxious. And how they use chatbots is tied to their mental health.

item.title: Florida sees spike in dengue fever cases
item.description: Florida is seeing a record number of dengue fever cases this year as the tropical disease thrives in warming climates.

item.title: What killed 500-plus penguins? How scientists solved the mystery
item.description: The penguins that perished lived on the Danger Islands in Antarctica. The prime suspect was avian flu. Researchers were surprised by what they found.

item.description: The campaign to defend access to transgender healthcare for young people in Missouri is taking an unhurried approach to talking with voters about the proposed ban.

item.title: New blood test can detect changes associated with Alzheimer's disease
item.description: Brain changes associated with Alzheimer's disease can be detected by a new type of blood test -- and a growing number of patients are asking their doctors about it.

item.title: Eleven states cut Medicaid coverage for refugees who are pregnant or children
item.description: When Congress cut Medicaid benefits for refugees who are in the U.S. legally, most states allowed them to continue for children and pregnant women. Arizona and 10 others did not.

item.title: Trump administration will allow pharmacies to make popular peptides
item.description: The Department of Health and Human Services will let small compounding pharmacies make six peptides that haven't been approved by the Food and Drug Administration. It may not be enough to meet demand.

item.title: Are you an organ donor? Here are some rule changes you may want to know
item.description: Transplant teams can talk to families about organ donation before they've decided whether to continue life-sustaining medical care for loved ones. Until now, that has been forbidden.
